newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico net assets rise to Dec 20.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico net assets rise to Dec 20.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said Tuesday that its net international assets as of Dec 20 were $5.585 billion, compared to $5.212 billion on Dec 13.
The central bank said that its net international reserves as of Dec 20 were $16.780 billion, compared to $16.344 billion as of Dec 13.
It said the increase of $373 million in international assets in the week was due to:
- Net revenues from operations with state oil firm Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) of $214 million;
- Net purchases of foreign currency from the federal government worth $144 million;
-purchases for $90 million from credit institutions from the dollar put option plan;

- A net loss of $75 million for a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts of commercial banks at the central bank.
The balance of the government's deposits with the central bank rose by 9.086 billion pesos, mainly as a result of tax collections.
Central bank credit to financial institutions rose by 10.549 billion pesos to compensate for the monetary impact of the tax collection and other factors.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's assets and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six month duration from other central banks.
